summary: CMS (Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services) said its enrollment freeze has blocked about 250 new home health agencies from Medicare.
CMS has suspended $1.4 billion in payments to hospice and home health providers, mostly in California.
CMS extended the freeze six months after the meeting but narrowed it so established operators can expand.
The final 2027 home health rule raises Medicare payments about 2.4%, the first increase after four years of cuts.

items.title: Medicare enrollment freeze on new home health agencies and hospices: CMS update at the opening keynote
lines: About 250 home health agencies and 50 hospices blocked from Medicare enrollment since the May 2026 freeze, per CMS chief operating officer (COO) Kim Brandt.
Brandt said billing dropped sharply in some areas, especially California hospice; figures not reported.
Brandt credited the savings with extending the Medicare trust fund's life and with this year's more favorable rates; dollar savings not reported.
Alliance government affairs chief Denis Fleming warned of rural access gaps from the nationwide freeze; figures not reported.

items.title: CMS payment suspensions against hospice and home health providers
lines: CMS has suspended payments to 899 hospice and home health providers, 812 of them in California.
$1.4 billion in total payments suspended to date, per Brandt.
Brandt conceded some good providers get caught; the share of legitimate providers affected was not reported.
Brandt said the decision to impose the freezes took CMS more than 1 year.

items.title: Freeze extended and narrowed after the meeting (CMS)
lines: The original 6-month freeze was due to expire on Nov. 13, 2026.
CMS extended the freeze by 6 months, modified so established providers can open new locations and expand services.
Alliance CEO Jennifer Sheets backed the narrower rules and urged targeted, data-driven enforcement over the next 6 months.
This loosens growth limits for established chains; the impact on specific companies was not reported.

items.title: Final 2027 Medicare home health payment rule (CMS)
lines: Total Medicare home health payments up about 2.4%, or $415 million, versus 2026; finalized Nov. 4, 2026.
The increase is a 2.1% base payment update ($365 million) plus 0.3% from an updated high-cost outlier threshold ($50 million).
Agencies that fail to report quality data get only a 0.1% update (2.1% minus 2 percentage points).
Most payment and quality changes take effect Jan. 1, 2027.

items.title: 2027 home health rule: temporary cut, reporting deadline and palliative care (CMS)
lines: A 3.0% temporary cut to the 30-day payment rate recovers about $500 million of $4.9 billion CMS considers past overpayments; no new permanent cut.
Agencies now have 45 days to submit and correct patient assessment data (the Outcome and Assessment Information Set, OASIS).
CMS clarified that palliative care can be delivered under the existing home health benefit, with no separate payment; figures not reported.
New provider enrollment and payment recovery rules apply across Medicare; savings estimated at about $82 million a year.

items.title: VITAS Healthcare (Chemed) on the opening panel and joining the Alliance board
lines: VITAS CEO Joel Wherley warned that suspicion of fraud makes hospice harder to discuss with families; figures not reported.
Wherley was named to the Alliance board on Nov. 5, 2026.
VITAS executive Patty Husted received the Alliance Lifetime Achievement Award in 2026.
No VITAS volume, rate or guidance figures were reported at the meeting.

items.title: Meeting footprint, AI focus and awards (Alliance; Aveanna Healthcare)
lines: More than 1,400 attendees and exhibitors, versus more than 1,700 at the first Alliance meeting in New Orleans in 2025.
A pre-conference workshop on technology and artificial intelligence (AI) for executives ran Oct. 27-28; adoption figures not reported.
Aveanna Healthcare government affairs VP Teri Henning was named 2026 Advocate of the Year.
The next annual meeting is in Seattle, Oct. 19-22, 2027.

expert_minds: Fraud enforcement and the enrollment freeze dominated the opening keynote: Kim Brandt (CMS), Denis Fleming and Jennifer Sheets (Alliance), Joel Wherley (VITAS).
Rural access gaps from a nationwide freeze, raised by Denis Fleming of the Alliance.
Using AI and technology in daily operations, per the Alliance meeting release and a pre-conference workshop for executives.
Home health, hospice, palliative, Medicaid home-based and personal care working as one community, with more clinical and operational content planned for 2027, per Alliance CEO Jennifer Sheets.
